hints: A permutation with no increasing or decreasing subsequence longer than k has at most k^2 elements.
Use decreasing blocks of consecutive increasing value ranges.
Make every block size at most k and use at most k blocks.
analogy: Within a block values fall, while moving between blocks values rise.
example: For n=5,k=3, blocks [3,2,1] and [5,4] give longest decreasing length 3 and longest increasing length 2.
algorithm: If n>k*k print IMPOSSIBLE. Otherwise partition 1 through n into consecutive blocks of size at most k, making the first block size k, and output each block in descending order while blocks appear in increasing value order.
correctness: An increasing subsequence uses at most one value per block; a decreasing subsequence stays within one block. There are at most k blocks and each has at most k elements, while the first block gives a decreasing subsequence of exactly k. The Erdos-Szekeres theorem rules out n>k^2.
complexity: For n and k, O(n) time and O(1) extra space excluding output.
